newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed in slow trade on Wednesday with sentiment cautious, traders said.
They said there were rumours that the central government had recently suspended some financial institutions from trading on the repo market for deferring payments for state debt trading.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 8.01 percent from 8.86 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 4.3 million lots from a thin 2.9 million lots on Tuesday.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The rumours made sentiment cautious, making most contracts consolidate on Tuseday and Wednesday," one trader said.
Traders said they expected the rates to move narrowly in the next few days but a large number of new domestic A share issues would support the three-day and seven-day contracts.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Wednesday but trading was more active than previous few days due to the forthcoming listing of a new three-year T-note next Monday, traders said.
The most actively traded three-year note that matures in August 1999 rose to 108.92 yuan from 108.74 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 1.1 million lots from 746,651 lots.
The latest batch of China's state debt, the three-year T-note that matures in May 2000 will be listed on Monday after its issue ending on May 31.
The forthcoming listing made trading in the existing three-year note more active, pushing up the volume.
Traders said they expected the contracts to rise slightly in the short term. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
